name: Local CI
description: Runs your GitHub workflow jobs on this machine's own Docker, from the session that is working on the code. It reports Docker in three states rather than two — missing, installed but the engine is not answering, or ready — checks that the engine runs Linux containers, and says whether the act runtime is on PATH, naming the install command when it is not. It reads the project's .github/workflows and says, per job, either that it can run here or the concrete reason it cannot: a matrix, a runner that is not Linux, artifacts exchanged with another job, or an action that only means something on GitHub. A job runs whole or not at all — anything it does not understand it refuses rather than guesses. A session can start a run itself and read the verdict back, with the operator approving the exact command each time, and a project can be set to hold back its pull requests until a local run has passed. The verdict is about this machine: act's images are not GitHub's, so it predicts the pull-request check rather than replacing it.
author: Cockpit
